title: WhiteMagic Memory Crystals
subtitle: signed-ciphertext audit without the key-encryption key
label: whitemagic-crystals+ciphertext-audit
measured_on: whitemagic crystal_client.py at 273b177b (sha256 e44b13f2), Python 3.12, macOS
What this means: A third party holding the signed ciphertext but not the key-encryption key runs LocalCrystalStore.verify_third_party() and is told about every one of the ten edits. It is an audit, not the read path: it shows that someone without the plaintext can check the store, not that the agent is stopped from reading an edited record. The row was narrowed to this from a plaintext read after a detached-plaintext case showed the earlier claim was too broad; the maintainer posted that correction to the W3C interop list himself.
Where the attacker stands: The attacker reads and writes the WhiteMagic store directory, as a mounted volume, a shared disk or a restored backup would allow. He holds no signing key. In the default and audit rows he cannot reach the anchors directory under XDG_STATE_HOME; in the in-store row the commitment sits inside the directory he controls. An attacker who holds a key or the anchors directory is a different measurement and these rows do not speak for it.
verdicts_intro:
Detection point: the audit, a separate call the operator has to make; the read path serves the edit first.

Level L0, Measured. The store has a published row. Any verdicts. What L0 means.
reproduce_intro: Everything runs offline. The run seeds a fresh store through the client's own API, applies each edit beneath it, reopens the store and records what came back.

export AGMI_WHITEMAGIC_CRYSTAL_CLIENT=<path to crystal_client.py>
python agmi/full_runner.py --json results/scorecard.json   # every row, this one included
python -m agmi.agent --target whitemagic-crystals+ciphertext-audit --compose
